name: movements-029
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: Dumbbell Step Ups. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs). Place the right foot on the elevated platform. Step on the platform by extending the hip and the knee of your right leg. Use the heel mainly to lift the rest of your body up and place the foot of the left leg on the platform as well. Breathe out as you execute the force required to come up. Step down with the left leg by flexing the hip and knee of the right leg as you inhale. Return to the original standing position by placing the right foot of to next to the left foot on the initial position. Repeat with the right leg for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.

Row 1 column 2: Dumbbell sumo deadlift. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Lower your dumbbell to the ground between your legs. Assume a wide stance and with a straight back squat down. With the dumbbell standing upright, grip it by the top of the ‘head’ (picture 1).Keeping your chest up and core braced, push the floor away, driving back upwards to a standing position (picture 2). Repeat. If you can easily achieve 20-30 reps, use two dumbbells.

Row 1 column 3: Dumbbell Thruster. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Start with the dumbbells resting on your shoulders and squat down. Push into standing and raise the dumbbells into an overhead position. Bring the dumbbells back to your shoulders and repeat.

Row 1 column 4: Dumbbell Tricep Extension -Pronated Grip. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Lie down on a flat bench holding two dumbbells directly above your shoulders. Your arms should be fully extended and form a 90 degree angle from your torso and the floor. The palms of your hands should be facing forward, and your elbows should be tucked in. This will be your starting position. Now, inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells until they are near your ears. Be sure to keep your upper arms stationary and your elbows tucked in. Then, exhale and use your triceps to return the weight to the starting position.

Row 2 column 1: Dumbbell Triceps Extension. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Position one dumbbell over head with both hands under inner plate (heart shaped grip). With elbows over head, lower forearm behind upper arm by flexing elbows. Flex wrists at bottom to avoid hitting dumbbell on back of neck. Raise dumbbell over head by extending elbows while hyperextending wrists. Return and repeat.

Row 2 column 2: Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: The Dumbbell Underhand Dead Row will involve the back, which means you can try a bit heavier weight. The catch is that you need to be able to control the weight for all the reps. 1. Start by holding a pair of dumbbells with your feet shoulder-wide apart and your knees slightly bent. 2. Hinge at your hips to lower your torse forward until it's almost parallel to the floor, keeping your back flat and maintaining a slight bend in your knees. 3. Exhale as you row the dumbbells to your sides up to chest height, leading with your elbows until your upper arms are just past parallel to the floor and the dumbbells are at ribcage level. 4. Slowly lower to the starting position and repeat. Keep your back flat all the time.

Row 2 column 3: Dumbbell wide bicep curls. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart and palms facing forward. Bend your elbows and lift the dumbbells to your shoulders. Slowly return and repeat.

Row 2 column 4: Dynamic Back Stretch. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart. This will be your starting position. Keeping your arms straight, swing them straight up in front of you 5-10 times, increasing the range of motion each time until your arms are above your head.

Row 3 column 1: Dynamic Chest Stretch. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Stand with your hands together, arms extended directly in front of you. This will be your starting position. Keeping your arms straight, quickly move your arms back as far as possible and back in again, similar to an exaggerated clapping motion. Repeat 5-10 times, increasing speed as you do so.

Row 3 column 2: Dynamic Planche. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: 1. Start in a plank position, with your hands directly under your shoulders and your feet hip-width apart. 2. Engage your core to keep your body in a straight line from head to toe. 3. From this position, bend your knees slightly and jump with both feet inward, bringing them as close to your core as possible 4. As soon as your feet touch the ground, push off forcefully to jump again and return to the starting plank position. 5. Continue repeating this jumping motion, maintaining control and core stability throughout the exercise. 6. Make sure to keep your breathing steady while jumping, breathing deeply and controlling your breathing. 7. Keep your gaze fixed on the ground to maintain proper spinal alignment. 8. Repeat the jumps for the desired length of time or the number of repetitions recommended for your workout program. 9. To finish the exercise, rest by releasing the plank position, then stretch if necessary to loosen your muscles.

Row 3 column 3: Dynamic side hold. Equipment: Kettlebell. Exercise guide: Sling a rubber band on a kettlebell and lift the kettlebell by the rubber band. Let it hang by your side and stand on one leg, switch leg while continuing hold. Repeat with other hand

Row 3 column 4: Easy Continuous Swim (Freestyle). Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Swim freestyle at a relaxed, steady pace without stopping — think conversation pace, not racing. Focus on smooth, even strokes rather than speed or breathing technique; this is just to get your body moving and your heart rate up.
